title: Follow-up from PR #201 review (frontend-indicator-seasons-badge-followups-followups): riskBreach.main/background WCAG contrast overclaim
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #201 (frontend-indicator-seasons-badge-followups-followups), tracked here so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: theme.ts's new riskBreach.main comment (and the corresponding frontend-indicator-seasons-badge-followups-followups `decisions` entry) both claim the new riskBreach.main (#d52651) 'clears both a >=15 ΔE margin from every other palette color and >=4.5:1 WCAG contrast against white and against `background` below'. Independently recomputed (same relativeLuminance/contrastRatio formulas theme.test.ts already uses): #d52651 vs riskBreach.background (#fdecea) is actually ~4.3459:1, below the 4.5:1 AA floor for normal text -- not the claimed >=4.5:1. This is not a regression from this PR (the pre-PR value, #d32f2f vs #fdecea, was ~4.3540:1, also failing, so the change is a wash on this specific pairing) but it is a new, false, permanently-recorded compliance claim in both a code comment and the task's decision-memory log. It matters in practice because components/common/RiskBreachBanner/RiskBreachBanner.tsx:37,41 paints theme.palette.riskBreach.main as 16px/fontWeight:700 text (below WCAG's ~18.7px bold 'large text' threshold, so the 4.5:1 normal-text minimum applies) directly onto theme.palette.riskBreach.background as the box fill -- a real, currently-shipping AA contrast gap that theme.test.ts's WCAG-contrast test block (added by frontend-indicator-seasons-badge-followups) never checks, since that block only covers the four season colors against white. Fix: (a) correct the false comment/decision claims to state the actual ~4.35:1 figure and that it's a known pre-existing gap, and (b) separately decide whether to actually close the gap (e.g. lighten riskBreach.background or further adjust riskBreach.main, while re-verifying the >=15 ΔE76 margins from every other palette color and the >=4.5:1 contrast against white are preserved) or explicitly accept it as a known limitation, and add a theme.test.ts assertion for the riskBreach.main-vs-background pairing either way so this doesn't silently drift again.

decisions.decision: Independently re-verified the contrast claim before touching anything: reimplemented theme.test.ts's exact relativeLuminance/contrastRatio formulas in a standalone script and computed contrastRatio('#d52651', '#fdecea') = 4.3459:1 (matches the task description's ~4.35:1 and the prior review chain's figure -- not overclaimed, not underclaimed). Chose option (a) (actually close the gap) rather than (b) (just fix the comment): darkened riskBreach.main from #d52651 to #cb244d, same hue (345.27deg -> 345.27deg) and saturation (69.7% -> 69.9%), lightness only (49.2% -> 46.9%) -- the same 'same hue/saturation, lower lightness' technique already used for the season colors. Verified the new value clears contrastRatio(main, background) = 4.7098:1 and contrastRatio(main, white) = 5.3862:1, both >=4.5:1 with real margin (not borderline), while every pairwise CIE76 ΔE from every other palette color stays >=18.6 (kangarooTail.main is the closest at 18.62, still well above the 15 floor; signal.sell is 20.89). Rejected (b) alone because the gap is easy to close without materially risking the ΔE guards (confirmed by scanning lightness from 49% down to 40% and checking both the contrast curve and the kangarooTail/sell ΔE curves before picking a value with comfortable margin on both), so there was no need to just document-and-accept a fixable AA violation on a currently-shipping banner. Also corrected the theme.ts comment's false '>=4.5:1 WCAG contrast against white and against background' claim (which was true against white at the old value but false against background) to state the actual verified numbers and explain the darkening step, and added a new theme.test.ts assertion (contrastRatio(riskBreach.main, riskBreach.background) >= 4.5 and contrastRatio(riskBreach.main, white) >= 4.5) so this pairing is now locked in by a test rather than only a comment.
decisions.rationale: Three prior rounds of this followup chain each had someone assert a contrast/distance number the next reviewer had to recompute and found wrong -- the task explicitly asked for independent re-verification before any change, so verifying first (and finding the ~4.35:1 figure accurate) was necessary before deciding whether a color change was even warranted, rather than trusting the description. Picking a lightness with real margin above both the 4.5:1 floor (4.71:1 chosen, not a borderline 4.51:1) and the 15 ΔE76 floor (18.6 minimum remaining, not a borderline 15.1) avoids leaving a value that could silently regress back under either floor from a future rounding change or reviewer's differently-rounded recomputation -- the exact failure mode that caused this three-round chain in the first place.

review.notes: Fourth round of this color-contrast followup chain, reviewed with maximum independent-verification scrutiny per the dispatch instructions (each of the prior three rounds had a numeric claim the next reviewer found wrong). Independently recomputed every claim from scratch, not reusing any script/computation from earlier in this session: (1) WCAG contrast via a from-scratch Python implementation of the W3C relative-luminance/contrast-ratio formula -- contrastRatio(#cb244d, #fdecea) = 4.7098:1 and contrastRatio(#cb244d, #ffffff) = 5.3862:1, both matching the PR's claimed figures exactly. (2) CIE76 ΔE76 via a from-scratch sRGB->linear->XYZ(D65)->Lab pipeline, computed against all 11 other palette colors: minimum is kangarooTail.main at 18.6230 (claimed '>=18.6, kangarooTail closest' -- exact match), signal.sell at 20.8874 (claimed 20.89 -- exact match), confirming no new collision anywhere including the signal.sell pairing that was PR #201's whole point. (3) Read theme.test.ts's new assertion directly: it calls contrastRatio(theme.palette.riskBreach.main, white) and contrastRatio(theme.palette.riskBreach.main, theme.palette.riskBreach.background), both >=4.5 -- live theme values, not hardcoded literals, so it will track any future drift rather than silently going stale like the comment-only claim did. (4) Converted both old (#d52651) and new (#cb244d) hex to HSL independently (colorsys-based, not reusing theme.ts's own conversion): H 345.26->345.27deg, S 69.72->69.87%, L 49.22->46.86% -- confirms the claimed 'same hue/saturation, lightness only' change is genuine, not a mischaracterized hue/saturation drift hiding behind a lightness framing. All four independently verified; nothing needed correction this round. Also ran: frontend vitest (687/687 pass, 99.64%/98.94% stmt/branch coverage), backend pytest (921/921 pass, 99.94% coverage, unaffected by this change but re-run per check-coverage), ruff+mypy (clean), eslint+tsc -b (clean), the code-review skill (0 findings), and a browser walkthrough via a real Chromium instance (Playwright, driven directly since no Playwright MCP tool was exposed in this session) against both RiskBreachBanner Storybook stories (Portfolio-page and Dashboard wording) -- computed styles confirm background rgb(253,236,234)/text+border rgb(203,36,77) matching #cb244d exactly, screenshot shows a clearly-legible danger/breach red, not washed out, no console errors, no failed network requests. Also ran the persisted e2e suite (make e2e): 16/16 specs pass across dashboard/navigation/portfolio/stock-analysis/watchlist. No API route or schema touched, so no OpenAPI snapshot check needed. No new/changed frontend components (theme.ts constant change only), so no common/-vs-feature placement question applies. The task's single checklist item is marked done with a decisions entry that documents the judgment call (fix the actual gap vs. just correct the false comment) and its rationale, satisfying CLAUDE.md's decision-memory requirement. No blocking or non-blocking findings this round -- this closes out the seasons-badge/riskBreach color-contrast followup chain (frontend-indicator-seasons-badge -> ...-followups -> ...-followups-followups -> this task).
